brief: Six negotiating habits that cost people money

slots.body: Six habits that decide what you get paid, none of which are about the quality of the work being discussed.
slots.item1: Why the first number spoken sets the range
slots.item2: The pause that costs more than any discount
slots.coverNote: The uncomfortable one is on the last page

slots.body: Not the price — the range. Every number that follows is read as a distance from the first one, which is why the opening figure does most of the work.
slots.p1Body: High enough to be argued with, not high enough to end the conversation.
slots.p2Body: A number delivered with a caveat has already been discounted.
slots.p3Body: Decided in advance, in writing, when you are not in the room.
slots.closingLine: An anchor you did not choose is an anchor somebody chose for you.

slots.body: The silence after a price feels far longer to the person who said it. Filling it is how a rate gets discounted before anyone has objected to it.
slots.p1Body: Explaining the number invites an argument about its parts.
slots.p2Body: Softening language tells them the figure is negotiable before they decide.
slots.p3Body: Whoever speaks next is usually the one who moves.
slots.closingLine: Most discounts are self-inflicted in the four seconds after the number.

slots.body: Dropping the figure while keeping the work teaches the other side that your first number was decoration. Moving both keeps the trade honest.
slots.p1Body: Every reduction comes out of what is included, visibly.
slots.p2Body: Two rounds becomes one. The number falls because the work did.
slots.p3Body: The removed piece stays priced, so adding it back is trivial.
slots.closingLine: Discounting the price alone prices everything you do afterwards.

slots.body: A deadline you did not set is a pressure applied to you. Naming it out loud usually reveals that it belongs to a launch or a board meeting rather than to the work.
slots.p1Body: Most deadlines have a reason, and the reason is negotiable.
slots.p2Body: Speed is a service. It should appear on the invoice as one.
slots.p3Title: Never be the last to know
slots.p3Body: A date announced late is a date you had no chance to shape.
slots.closingLine: The person under time pressure is the one who concedes, every time.

slots.body: Most disputes are not about the price at all. They are about what was assumed on either side and written down by neither, which surfaces the week before delivery.
slots.p1Body: The list of what you are not doing protects the relationship most.
slots.p2Body: It funds the work and it filters out the people who were never going to pay.
slots.p3Body: A price with no expiry is one you will honour in a year at today's rate.
slots.closingLine: Every unbilled hour started as an assumption nobody said out loud.

slots.body: Negotiation raises what people will pay for a given standard. It does not raise the standard, and a client who feels overcharged does not come back or refer you.
slots.p1Body: Charge above what you deliver and the market corrects within two projects.
slots.p2Body: Your real rate is what your last satisfied client says you are worth.
slots.p3Body: Increase until you feel resistance. That edge is the actual number.
slots.closingLine: Pricing is a lagging indicator of the work, and it always catches up.

slots.eyebrow: On the next proposal, not the current one
slots.body: Not a new rate, not a rehearsed speech. One number, said plainly, followed by nothing at all until they answer.
slots.closingLine: The four seconds you find hardest are the four that decide the figure.
